newsitem.title: CHINA: China's South China Sea oil production up in '96.
newsitem.headline: China's South China Sea oil production up in '96.

text.p: China's oilfields in the South China Sea produced almost 1.2 million tonnes of crude oil in January, the official Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
In 1996, Chinese oilfields in the South China Sea produced a record of over 11.84 million tonnes of crude oil, doubling that of the previous year, Xinhua said, quoting the South China Sea Eastern Co.
The company, which is in charge of China's oilfields in the South China Sea, has discovered geological crude oil reserves of 500 million tonnes since it was founded in 1983.
Nine oilfields have proved to be commercially worthy of exploration. Eight have been put into operation with the ninth still under construction.
